questions.question: What makes CSS custom properties fundamentally different from Sass (`$variable`) variables?
options: Custom properties require a build step and Sass variables don't

Custom properties are a real part of the CSS language and can change at runtime (via class toggles, media queries, or JavaScript); Sass variables are replaced with literal values at compile time and can't
There is no real difference between the two
Sass variables can be read by JavaScript but custom properties cannot
questions.explanation: Sass variables are resolved once during compilation; CSS custom properties remain live values in the browser that respond to the cascade, media queries, and JS.

questions.question: Why can redeclaring `--color-bg` inside a `.dark-theme` class instantly theme a whole page?
options: It requires a full page reload to take effect
Elements inside .dark-theme pick up the new cascaded value of --color-bg automatically, the same way any other inherited CSS property would update
Dark mode requires a separate JavaScript library
Custom properties can only be declared once per page
questions.explanation: Custom properties follow the normal CSS cascade — redeclaring one at a more specific selector overrides it for everything inside that selector, live, with no rebuild.

questions.question: In `background: var(--badge-color, #71717a);`, when does the fallback `#71717a` get used?
options: Only when --badge-color is set to a falsy value like 0
The fallback is always applied regardless of --badge-color
Fallback values are not supported by var()
questions.explanation: var()'s second argument is used only when the custom property is undefined, making components safely usable even where the variable was never declared.

questions.question: What is one thing a CSS custom property can do that a Sass variable fundamentally cannot?
options: Be read and updated at runtime from JavaScript via element.style.setProperty()
Be used inside a CSS selector
Be declared more than once in a stylesheet
questions.explanation: Because custom properties exist in the browser's rendering, JavaScript can read and write them live; a Sass variable has already disappeared into literal values by the time the browser sees the CSS.
